newsitem.title: GERMANY: Military officials lay out approaches on Zaire aid.
newsitem.headline: Military officials lay out approaches on Zaire aid.

text.p: Military officials on Sunday said they had mapped out ways of providing humanitarian relief to refugees in Zaire ranging from a low level of assistance to using security forces as protection.

Lieutenant-General Maurice Baril of Canada, who would lead any multinational force to help refugees in eastern Zaire, said the meeting of military leaders agreed that as many as 250,000 refugees might still be in eastern Zaire.
Baril said military planners at the meeting, which began on Friday, estimated that about 575,000 refugees had so far returned to Rwanda.
He said up to 300,000 refugees more could still be in eastern Zaire but that the figure had not been confirmed.

"The mission of a multinational force, as we have defined it, would be to facilitate the delivery of humanitarian assistance and voluntary repatriation of refugees and displaced persons," Baril said in a statement at a news conference.
"The objectives of such a force would be strictly humanitarian. The force would be politically and militarily neutral," Baril said.
He did not provide details about possible forces, including contributions from nations attending the meeting, and said individual goverments must now review the mission options.
The options range from continuing to encourage current humanitarian assistance and the voluntary repatriation of refugees to using "security forces" to provide protection.

Another option calls for the multinational force headquarters to direct and coordinate humanitarian efforts, while another calls for "facilitating humanitarian assistance and voluntary repatriation in a non-threatening environment".
Baril did not say where the missions could be based in the region but Zaire has welcomed calls for military help while Rwanda has said the mission was unnecessary.
"The tasks of such a force would be considerable and complex," Baril said, adding he would now return to central Africa to continue contingency planning for any mission.
He also reaffirmed that the mandate for the mission would end on March 31, 1997 and that, if required, responsibility would be passed onto a follow-on organisation.
